sentence: This project studies the cells and molecules involved in major depressive disorder using postmortem brain tissue.
This project studies how a mutation helps papillomavirus cause disease, looking at immune cells and keratinocytes.
This project builds a 3D atlas of the aging human intestine using imaging and computational tools.
This project tries to develop drugs that target a protein in the transcription machinery for acute myeloid leukemia.
This project provides microscopes and image analysis tools to study changes linked to neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project measures many kinds of molecules in human brain tissue and blood to find subtypes of Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies dorsal root ganglion neurons in models of knee osteoarthritis pain.
This project studies how age-related changes in the prefrontal cortex relate to Alzheimer's disease.
This project tests how the acid, base and salt parts of e-cigarettes affect health during pregnancy.
This project studies how cancer cells and the immune response work in order to develop ways to treat cancer.
This project tests three treatment strategies for prostate cancer in clinical trials and laboratory studies.
This project studies the cells that make antibodies to understand how some protect against infection and others cause disease.
This project studies what recovery support and treatments colleges and universities offer for alcohol-related problems.
This project studies how one protein affects alpha-synuclein and its role in Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia.
This project studies how alcohol changes the release of a neuropeptide in brain circuits of Drosophila and how this affects tolerance and sleep.
This project tests which cellular mechanisms change how mutations in the mitochondrial genome show up.
This project builds and tests 3D-printed vascular scaffolds that slowly degrade and carry drugs.
This project works to improve tests that find and identify microbes that cause infection, including fungal pathogens.
This project tries to find the molecules that let heart pacemaker cells sense mechanical stretch.
This project studies how the aryl hydrocarbon receptor in airway smooth muscle affects inflammation and airway changes in asthma.
